tips:
## The Vav-Consecutive (ו"ו ההיפוך)

The vav-consecutive is the primary narrative tense of biblical Hebrew. It attaches **וַ** (vav with patach and dagesh) to a future-form verb, converting it to past meaning:

| Future Form | With Vav-Consecutive | Meaning |
|------------|---------------------|----------|
| יֹאמַר (he will say) | וַיֹּאמֶר | and he said |
| יִהְיֶה (it will be) | וַיְהִי | and it was |
| יֵלֵךְ (he will go) | וַיֵּלֶךְ | and he went |

This creates chains of sequential narrative events:
- וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים: יְהִי אוֹר. וַיְהִי אוֹר.
- And God said: Let there be light. And there was light.

## Key Biblical Vocabulary

- **בְּרֵאשִׁית** -- In the beginning (the first word of the Torah)
- **אֶרֶץ** -- Land, earth (appears over 2,500 times in the Bible)
- **שָׁמַיִם** -- Heavens, sky
- **נֶפֶשׁ** -- Soul, life, being
- **הָלוֹךְ** -- The infinitive absolute, used for emphasis: הָלוֹךְ הָלַךְ = he walked and walked

Modern Hebrew does not use the vav-consecutive productively, but knowing it unlocks the Torah, prayers, and literary Hebrew.
